q: Conservation means keeping and protecting a living and changing ____.
e: Conservation means keeping and protecting a living and changing environment. The blank is environment.

q: Active intervention is required to restore areas and to protect native species, and sustainable benefits for the present as well as future ____.
e: Active intervention is required to restore areas and to protect native species, and sustainable benefits for the present as well as future strategies. Write strategies in the gap.

q: Narrowly Utilitarian reason for conservation involves useful human products like food, fibres, drugs and medicines obtained from ____.
e: Narrowly Utilitarian reason for conservation involves useful human products like food, fibres, drugs and medicines obtained from biodiversity. The blank is biodiversity.

q: Broadly Utilitarian reason for conservation involves ecosystem services like providing oxygen, pollinating crops and controlling floods, ____, etc.
e: Broadly Utilitarian reason for conservation involves ecosystem services like providing oxygen, pollinating crops and controlling floods, erosions, etc. That missing piece is erosions.

q: Ethical Utilitarian reason for conservation states that every living species has an intrinsic value and every species has the right to ____.
e: Ethical Utilitarian reason for conservation states that every living species has an intrinsic value and every species has the right to live. That missing piece is live.

q: In situ methods are the ways of conservation of species which take place in the natural ____ of the organism.
e: In situ methods are the ways of conservation of species which take place in the natural habitat of the organism. The blank is habitat.

q: Nature reserves such as wildlife sanctuary, national park and biosphere reserve help endangered species by maintaining their habitat and genetic ____.
e: Nature reserves such as wildlife sanctuary, national park and biosphere reserve help endangered species by maintaining their habitat and genetic diversity. Write diversity in the gap.

q: Keeping these organisms in situ means putting them in the ecosystem where they belong, allowing them to continue to adapt without interference from outside ____.
e: Keeping these organisms in situ means putting them in the ecosystem where they belong, allowing them to continue to adapt without interference from outside influences. Write influences in the gap.

q: Ex situ methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants outside their natural ____.
e: Ex situ methods are the ways to conserve animals and plants outside their natural habitats. Write habitats in the gap.

q: Zoos and wildlife parks used to exist just for people to look at the animals, but today they are very important in animal conservation by ex situ conservation ____.
e: Zoos and wildlife parks used to exist just for people to look at the animals, but today they are very important in animal conservation by ex situ conservation methods. Write methods in the gap.

q: The three methods of ex situ conservation are captive breeding of animals, storage of seeds in the seed bank and cultivation of plants in botanical ____.
e: The three methods of ex situ conservation are captive breeding of animals, storage of seeds in the seed bank and cultivation of plants in botanical garden. That missing piece is garden.

q: In captive breeding programmes, individuals of an endangered species are bred in zoos and parks in an attempt to save the species from ____.
e: In captive breeding programmes, individuals of an endangered species are bred in zoos and parks in an attempt to save the species from extinction. That missing piece is extinction.

q: Usually, the ultimate aim of captive breeding is to reintroduce the captive-bred animals into the wild to restore the original ____.
e: Usually, the ultimate aim of captive breeding is to reintroduce the captive-bred animals into the wild to restore the original populations. Write populations in the gap.

q: Reintroduction does not always work, but it can be successful in national parks or other protected ____.
e: Reintroduction does not always work, but it can be successful in national parks or other protected areas. Write areas in the gap.

q: Techniques used in captive breeding include artificial insemination, embryo transfer to a surrogate mother, cryogenics, human-raised young, and keeping a ____.
e: Techniques used in captive breeding include artificial insemination, embryo transfer to a surrogate mother, cryogenics, human-raised young, and keeping a pedigree. That missing piece is pedigree.

q: Cryogenics involves freezing eggs, sperm cells and embryos for future ____.
e: Cryogenics involves freezing eggs, sperm cells and embryos for future use. Write use in the gap.

q: Keeping a pedigree helps prevent ____ in captive breeding programmes.
e: Keeping a pedigree helps prevent inbreeding in captive breeding programmes. Write inbreeding in the gap.

q: It has been estimated that ____ of the world's flowering plant species could disappear within the next 50 years.
e: It has been estimated that 25\% of the world's flowering plant species could disappear within the next 50 years. The blank is 25\%.

q: Seeds in a seed bank are kept in cold, dark conditions in which the metabolism of the seed slows down so the seed is prevented from ____.
e: Seeds in a seed bank are kept in cold, dark conditions in which the metabolism of the seed slows down so the seed is prevented from germinating. That missing piece is germinating.

q: Seeds collected for a seed bank are dried, then stored, and seed ____ is tested at regular intervals.
e: Seeds collected for a seed bank are dried, then stored, and seed germination is tested at regular intervals. Write germination in the gap.

q: Seeds in a seed bank are stored in a temperature of ____ and in dark conditions.
e: Seeds in a seed bank are stored in a temperature of -14^\circ C and in dark conditions. That missing piece is -14^\circ C.

q: The storage of seeds is one of the most widespread and valuable ex situ approaches to ____.
e: The storage of seeds is one of the most widespread and valuable ex situ approaches to conservation. That missing piece is conservation.

q: Saved and viable seeds in a seed bank contain a treasure trove of useful genes that breeders can use for developing improved varieties of our major food ____.
e: Saved and viable seeds in a seed bank contain a treasure trove of useful genes that breeders can use for developing improved varieties of our major food crops. That missing piece is crops.

q: About ____ plant species are grown in private gardens, arboretums and botanical gardens all over the world.
e: About 80,000 plant species are grown in private gardens, arboretums and botanical gardens all over the world. That missing piece is 80,000.

q: Botanical gardens not only serve as taxonomic and systematic research centers but they play an important role as valuable sources of plant ____.
e: Botanical gardens not only serve as taxonomic and systematic research centers but they play an important role as valuable sources of plant ecology. Write ecology in the gap.

q: One of the major objectives of botanical gardens is to create and support collections of native taxa, and to build and maintain stocks of plants for ex situ conservation and sustainable utilization of plant ____.
e: One of the major objectives of botanical gardens is to create and support collections of native taxa, and to build and maintain stocks of plants for ex situ conservation and sustainable utilization of plant resources. Write resources in the gap.

q: Protected areas (PAs) are important tools for biodiversity conservation and sustainable ____.
e: Protected areas (PAs) are important tools for biodiversity conservation and sustainable development. Write development in the gap.

q: PAs safeguard ecosystems and their services, such as water provision, food production, carbon sequestration and climate ____.
e: PAs safeguard ecosystems and their services, such as water provision, food production, carbon sequestration and climate regulation. The blank is regulation.

q: PAs preserve the integrity of spiritual and cultural values placed by indigenous people on wild areas and offer opportunities of inspiration, study and ____.
e: PAs preserve the integrity of spiritual and cultural values placed by indigenous people on wild areas and offer opportunities of inspiration, study and recreation. Write recreation in the gap.

q: In Myanmar, ____ protected areas have been established.
e: In Myanmar, 42 protected areas have been established. The blank is 42.

q: A scientific reserve is held for the protection of their features for scientific study, research, education, and the benefit of the ____.
e: A scientific reserve is held for the protection of their features for scientific study, research, education, and the benefit of the country. Write country in the gap.

q: A national park is an area set aside by a national government for the preservation of the natural ____.
e: A national park is an area set aside by a national government for the preservation of the natural environment. The blank is environment.

q: No settlement or resource harvesting is allowed in a national park, but visitors are ____.
e: No settlement or resource harvesting is allowed in a national park, but visitors are permitted. That missing piece is permitted.

q: A marine park is a permanent marine reservation for the conservation of ____.
e: A marine park is a permanent marine reservation for the conservation of species. That missing piece is species.

q: Lampi Island Marine National Park is an example of a marine national park in Myanmar, which is the same as national park but in marine, island and coastal ____.
e: Lampi Island Marine National Park is an example of a marine national park in Myanmar, which is the same as national park but in marine, island and coastal environments. That missing piece is environments.

q: A nature reserve is a protected area of importance for flora, fauna, or features of geological or other special ____.
e: A nature reserve is a protected area of importance for flora, fauna, or features of geological or other special interest. Write interest in the gap.

q: A wildlife sanctuary is an area where animal habitats and their surroundings are protected from any sort of ____.
e: A wildlife sanctuary is an area where animal habitats and their surroundings are protected from any sort of disturbance. The blank is disturbance.

q: The capturing, killing and poaching of animals is strictly ____ in wildlife sanctuaries.
e: The capturing, killing and poaching of animals is strictly prohibited in wildlife sanctuaries. Write prohibited in the gap.

q: In the early 1990s, the Government of Myanmar introduced Community forest (CF) as a way to protect endangered forest resources and support the subsistence needs of rural ____.
e: In the early 1990s, the Government of Myanmar introduced Community forest (CF) as a way to protect endangered forest resources and support the subsistence needs of rural communities. Write communities in the gap.

q: Community forest means all sustainable forest management and utilization activities, in which the local community itself is ____.
e: Community forest means all sustainable forest management and utilization activities, in which the local community itself is involved. Write involved in the gap.
